farmer.evidence: Wide straw hat and big hoe read at every distance

miner.evidence: Yellow hardhat and pickaxe clear at 40; tiny yellow dot at 170

woodcutter.evidence: Orange beanie and axe read at 40; blends with hauler's orange at 170

blacksmith.evidence: Dark cap, small hammer; dark body gets lost on the grass

merchant.evidence: Purple hat and body, gold scales; purple stays visible

healer.evidence: White cap, small green cross and staff; faint at distance

soldier.evidence: Spear, red plume and steel helmet; tallest figure

builder.evidence: Teal cap and mallet; teal dot is distinct but tiny

hauler.evidence: Orange cap and sack on back; reads only from behind

idle.evidence: Plain brown bun-head; defined only by lacking a tool

governor.evidence: Crown, gold staff and red robe; red merges with the mantles

defects: Aerial and lineup sheets: at 170 studs the figures are about 10 px tall. Hats and tools are a few pixels, so most identities cannot be told apart without the name labels. Hauler and woodcutter (orange) and builder (teal) are the only clear colour cues.

Identity and silhouette sheets: the farmer, miner and woodcutter silhouettes are close. All three carry a large tool plus a hat blob, and the hat shapes are only faintly different. The miner, woodcutter and builder share nearly the same body block.

Identity and silhouette sheets: the healer, idle, builder, merchant and blacksmith have small, similar silhouettes. Their hats are small and some tools are held to the side, so they are hard to separate at 40 studs in the turned view.

Aerial sheet: the red mantle dominates every citizen, including the governor and soldier. It hides job colour from above, and the blacksmith and idle dark bodies vanish into shadow, so the 170-stud view has weak colour-value separation per job.

Variation sheet: citizens of the same job differ only by skin, hair and outfit tint. Rows of farmers and builders look nearly identical in the AFTER grid. The same hat, tool and pose repeat, so there is little individual variation in silhouette.
notes: The AFTER kit is a real improvement over BEFORE. Farmer, soldier, miner (hat) and builder (cap colour) now read, and the colours are better. The identities still don't separate reliably from the aerial camera: the healer, blacksmith and idle citizen disappear, and the red mantle swamps the colour cues. Same-job variation and silhouette difference at 40 studs stay below the pass bar of 4.
